title: Read and write any field

blocks.text: To reach a private field: find it with **`getDeclaredField`** (`getField` sees public fields only), call **`setAccessible(true)`**, then `get` or `set`. For a static field pass `null` as the instance. `getDeclaredField` does not look in superclasses, so an inherited field needs a **walk up the hierarchy**.

items: `read(target, name)`: the value of the field `name` of `target`, declared on its class or **any superclass**, at any access level. Primitives come back boxed.
`readStatic(type, name)`: the value of a static field of `type`.
A field that exists on no class of the hierarchy is a **`NoSuchFieldException`**.

cases.says: On a class with public fields: read gives a field's value (boxed for int, null for an unset reference), write changes it, readStatic reads a static field.
read finds and reads the private fields of an Account.
write changes an Account's private balance.
read(savings, "owner") finds the private owner field that Savings inherits from Account.
A field that exists nowhere in the hierarchy is a NoSuchFieldException.

concepts: getDeclaredField does not search superclasses, so an inherited field is found by walking the hierarchy.
A private field is read or written by finding it with getDeclaredField, calling setAccessible(true), then get or set.
A static field or method is used through reflection with null as the instance.
